extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria for determining, asserting, and maintaining small-entity and micro-entity status to permit payment of reduced USPTO patent fees, plus refund and error-correction procedures. Covers definitions, who may sign assertions, permissible assertion methods, government-use exceptions, fraud, and micro-entity income/filing limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of small entity (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A small entity means any party (person, small business concern, or nonprofit organization) under paragraphs (a)(1) through (a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All three categories (person, small business concern, nonprofit organization) are separate routes to qualify; definitions and additional conditions for each are specified in subparagraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person (individual) qualification for small entity
rubrics_metrics.description: A person means any inventor or other individual who has not assigned, granted, conveyed, or licensed, and is under no obligation to assign, grant, convey, or license, any rights in the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An inventor who has transferred some rights can still qualify if all parties who received rights also qualify as small entities under this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business concern definition and size standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A small business concern is a business that (i) has not assigned/licensed rights to a party that would not qualify as a small entity and (ii) meets the size standards in 13 CFR 121.801–121.805.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions about size standards can be directed to the SBA Size Standards Staff; assignment/licensing to a non-qualifying party disqualifies the business unless that party also qualifies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprofit organization definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprofit organization must (i) not have assigned/licensed rights to a party that would not qualify and (ii) be either: (A) a university or other institution of higher education, (B) a 501(c)(3) organization exempt under 501(a), (C) a nonprofit scientific or educational organization under state nonprofit statutes (35 U.S.C. 201(i)), or (D) a foreign nonprofit that would qualify if located in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All parties holding rights must qualify; the listed types are the recognized nonprofit categories for small-entity purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Government use license exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain government-use licenses or rights do not preclude claiming small entity status where specific statutory or Executive Order-based conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: rights determinations under Executive Order 10096 (§501.6), Federal agency action under 15 U.S.C. 3710d(a) allowing employee-inventor to retain title, retention under 35 U.S.C. 202(d) where the license is equivalent to 202(c)(4), funding agreements under 35 U.S.C. 202(c)(4) if the invention was made solely by employees of the small business/nonprofit or if the agency assigns/license rights as described, and CRADA-related provisions under 15 U.S.C. 3710a(b)(2)/(b)(3)(D) provided the lab has waived/assigned government ownership rights. Regardless of exception applicability, no refund under § 1.28(a) is available for any patent fee paid by the Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security interest does not equal obligation to assign (unless defaulted)
rubrics_metrics.description: A security interest is not considered an obligation to transfer rights in the invention for purposes of (a)(1)–(a)(3) unless the security interest has been defaulted upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple security interests (e.g., liens) do not disqualify small-entity status absent default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of small entity status permits reduced fees
rubrics_metrics.description: A party who properly asserts entitlement to small entity status will be accorded that status in the particular application or patent, allowing payment of certain reduced patent fees pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 41(h)(1) and reduced filing fees for electronic submissions under 35 U.S.C. 41(h)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishment is application/patent-specific; electronic filing of an original utility application with a proper assertion permits reduced filing fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to determine entitlement and to assert small entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party should determine entitlement pursuant to paragraph (a) and must make an assertion of entitlement to be accorded small entity status in the manner set forth in paragraphs (c)(1) or (c)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior determination that all parties holding rights qualify should be made before asserting small-entity status; the Office generally will not question proper assertions but fraud provisions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion by writing: content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A written assertion must be clearly identifiable, be signed, and convey the concept of entitlement to small entity status (e.g., state that applicant is a small entity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No specific words are required; the intent to assert small-entity status must be clearly indicated to comply. Signature requirements are set out in (c)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign a written assertion
rubrics_metrics.description: A written assertion may be signed by: (i) the applicant (§ 1.42 or § 1.421), (ii) a patent practitioner of record or practitioner acting under § 1.34, (iii) the inventor or joint inventor if the inventor is the applicant, or (iv) the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-AIA text includes additional filing signatory exceptions (e.g., parties identified in § 1.33(b), certain inventors, partial assignees with conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion by payment of specific small-entity fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment by any party of the exact amount of listed small-entity basic filing/transmittal/international search/basic national fees (specified sections) will be treated as a written assertion of entitlement to small entity status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of the exact small-entity basic filing fees in §§ 1.16(a)–(e), transmittal fees in § 1.445(a)(1) or § 1.1031(a), certain international search fees, or small-entity basic national fee in § 1.492(a) will be treated as an assertion even if the fee type was selected in error. If the Office accords status based on an inapplicable payment, any remaining applicable balance plus surcharges (§ 1.16(f)/(g)) will be due. Payment of small-entity fees other than the listed types, even if exact, will not be treated as an assertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion required in related, continuing, and reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Small-entity status must be specifically established by an assertion in each related, continuing, and reissue application in which status is desired; status in one application or patent does not affect others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refiling under § 1.53 as a continuation, divisional, CIP, or filing a reissue application requires a new assertion for the continuing/reissue application.

rubrics_metrics.name: When small-entity fee amounts can be paid
rubrics_metrics.description: Any fee other than the small-entity basic filing fees and the small-entity national fees of paragraph (c)(3) can be paid in the small-entity amount only if submitted with, or subsequent to, a written assertion of entitlement, except when refunds are permitted by § 1.28(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing of written assertion relative to fee payment matters for eligibility of reduced amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only one assertion required per application (and withdrawal rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: An assertion need be filed only once in an application or patent; once established, small-entity status remains in effect until changed pursuant to paragraph (g)(1). Where assignment to other small entities occurs after assertion, a second assertion is not required. Once withdrawn per (g)(2), a new written assertion is required to obtain small-entity status again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An assertion continues to cover subsequent payments in that application until the specific events requiring reassessment (issue/maintenance fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion requires reasonable prior determination of entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to submitting an assertion in any application (including related/continuing/reissue applications), a determination of entitlement should be made pursuant to paragraph (a); it should be determined that all parties holding rights qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office generally will not question proper assertions but retains the ability to do so; see the fraud provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: New determination and notification required at issue/maintenance fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Once status is established in an application or patent, small-entity fees may be paid without regard to a change in status until the issue fee or any maintenance fee is due. A new determination is needed when issue/maintenance fees are due. Notification of a loss of entitlement must be filed prior to or at the time of paying the earliest of the issue fee or any maintenance fee due after the date on which small-entity status is no longer appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notification of loss must be signed by a party identified in § 1.33(b). Payment of a fee in other than the small-entity amount is NOT sufficient notification that status is no longer appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud on the Office re small-entity assertions/payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any attempt to fraudulently establish small-entity status or to pay fees as a small entity, or improperly establishing status or paying fees with intent to deceive, shall be considered fraud practiced or attempted on the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent to deceive is dispositive; fraudulent acts will be treated as fraud on the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund eligibility when small-entity status later established
rubrics_metrics.description: A refund based on later establishment of small-entity status for fees timely paid in full prior to establishing status may only be obtained if an assertion under § 1.27(c) and a refund request are filed within three months of the date of the timely payment of the full fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three-month period is not extendable under § 1.136. Failure to establish status prior to, at the time of paying, or within three months of payment waives small-entity status for that fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of payment rules for refunds/deficiency calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The three-month refund-request period begins on the date that a full fee has been paid. The date a deficiency payment is paid in full determines the amount of deficiency owed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the actual payment dates to determine refund windows and deficiency amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excusing errors in small-entity status established in good faith (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: If small-entity status was established and small-entity fees paid in good faith but later discovered to be in error, the error will be excused upon compliance with separate submission/itemization requirements and payment of the deficiency owed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance requires a separate submission for each application/patent and full payment plus itemization; see sub-criteria for calculation and itemization details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate submission required per application/patent for error excusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Any paper submitted to excuse an error under § 1.28(c) must be limited to the deficiency payment for one application or one patent; separate submissions and itemizations are required for each application or patent involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.4(b) re separate submissions; do not combine multiple applications/patents on one submission for deficiency payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of deficiency owed when small-entity fees were erroneously paid
rubrics_metrics.description: The deficiency owed equals the difference between the current non-small-entity fee amount on the date the deficiency is paid in full and the amount of the previously erroneous small-entity fee payment. The total deficiency is the sum of individual deficiencies for each fee previously erroneously paid. If the fee paid in error was later subject to a fee decrease, the deficiency owed equals the amount previously paid in error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate each individual deficiency using current non-small amounts at payment date; sum them to obtain total deficiency owed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Itemization requirements for deficiency payment
rubrics_metrics.description: An itemization of the total deficiency payment is required and must include: (A) each particular type of fee erroneously paid as a small entity along with the current non-small-entity fee amount; (B) the small-entity fee actually paid and when paid; (C) the deficiency owed amount for each fee; and (D) the total deficiency payment owed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Itemization lets the Office differentiate identical-fee types paid on different dates; provide clear per-fee breakdowns and totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to comply with deficiency submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the requirements for separate submissions and itemizations are not complied with, the Office will either process the deficiency payment and charge the processing fee in § 1.17(i) or require compliance within a one-month non-extendable period under § 1.136(a) to avoid return of the deficiency paper, at the Office's option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliant submissions risk extra processing fees or return of the submission unless corrected within one month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deficiency payment operates as notification of loss of status
rubrics_metrics.description: Any deficiency payment submitted under § 1.28(c) (based on previous erroneous payment of a small-entity fee) will be treated under § 1.27(g)(2) as a notification of a loss of entitlement to small-entity status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting a deficiency both corrects fees and notifies the Office that small-entity status no longer applies for the relevant application/patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-entity status: baseline certification requirements (type A)
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish micro-entity status an applicant must certify: (1) they qualify as a small entity without relying on a government-use-license exception; (2) neither applicant nor inventor/joint inventor has been named on more than four previously filed patent applications (with certain exclusions); (3) neither applicant nor inventor/joint inventor had gross income in the preceding calendar year exceeding three times the median household income for that year; and (4) neither applicant nor inventor/joint inventor has assigned or is obligated to assign rights in the application to an entity whose prior-year gross income exceeded three times the median household income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The count of previously filed applications excludes foreign applications, provisional applications under 35 U.S.C. 111(b), or international applications where the basic national fee under 35 U.S.C. 41(a) was not paid. Income thresholds use the Census-reported median household income; see paragraph (c) for currency conversion rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-entity: exclusion where inventor assigned due to previous employment
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant/inventor is not considered to be named on a previously filed application for purposes of the four-application limit if the applicant/inventor has assigned, or is under an obligation to assign, all ownership rights in the prior application as a result of previous employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments required by prior employment remove those prior applications from the micro-entity counting restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-entity income conversion for non-USD incomes
rubrics_metrics.description: If gross income is not in U.S. dollars, the IRS average currency exchange rate during the preceding calendar year shall be used to determine whether income exceeds the threshold in paragraph (a)(3) or (a)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the IRS published average exchange rate for the relevant calendar year when converting foreign-currency incomes for threshold comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-entity alternative basis: institution of higher education (type B)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant can establish micro-entity status by certifying (1) qualification as a small entity without relying on government-use license exceptions and (2) either (i) the applicant's employer (from which the majority of income is obtained) is an institution of higher education as defined in 20 U.S.C. 1001(a), or (ii) the applicant has assigned or is under obligation to assign rights in the particular application to such an institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides an alternate path to micro-entity status tied to affiliation with an institution of higher education.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to establish micro-entity status (form and signature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Micro-entity status is established by filing a micro-entity certification in writing complying with either paragraph (a) or (d) and signed in compliance with § 1.33(b) (or appropriate representation rules for international filings). Status must be specifically established in each related, continuing, and reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International filings filed in a Receiving Office other than the U.S. must follow § 1.455/§ 1.1041 representation provisions when filing micro-entity certifications with the IB. Status in one application/patent does not carry over to related applications; each requires its own certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-entity fee payment allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee may be paid in the micro-entity amount when micro-entity status is properly established as provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text continues beyond the chunk, but the rule authorizes payment at the micro-entity reduced rate once certification is filed per requirements.
